clue.text: Red wine covers fashionable instrument that makes very low sounds
Stick with retrograde policy for a bar, conceivably

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backward, so the phrase it describes is read in reverse

parts.note: 'no tab' is a plausible bar rule: pay as you go, no running bill

explanation.surface: A pub sticks to an old-fashioned house rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceivably' warns that the policy is an invented example, not a fixed term.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's.

clue.text: Street gag for a while: …

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A street comedian keeps a joke running for some time, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but means to heave; the trailing dots carry the surface on into 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a continuous period of time, as in 'for a stretch'.

clue.text: …prance about without a bit of nervousness!

definitions.text: …prance about without a bit of nervousness!

indicators.note: about means around and about, so the letters of the word before are turned round into a new order
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out
a bit of a word is just one of its letters, here the first

explanation.surface: Continuing the street act: dance about freely, without a trace of stage fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also making it: drop the N from PRANCE and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or dance about playfully, which is what carefree prancing looks like.

clue.text: For Aaron, the first will be last — that's a symbol of life

indicators.note: the opening letter is sent to the back of the word, echoing the biblical saying

parts.note: Hank Aaron was a record-setting American baseball player

explanation.surface: A biblical saying about Moses' brother Aaron and a sacred emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: Aaron suggests the biblical priest, but here it is the baseball star Hank Aaron, so the first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh, a cross topped with a loop, was the ancient Egyptian hieroglyph for life.

clue.text: Second cousin's tantalizing, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the answer is part of the words before it

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A second cousin is rather tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second cousin' reads as a relative, but Second is the definition, on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A second and an instant are both very short moments of time.

clue.text: Something that's always popular: horrific revenge involving emergency room

indicators.note: involving means wrapping up within, so one part sits inside the other
something horrific is twisted and deformed, so the letters of the next word are distorted into a new order

parts.note: ER is the US abbreviation for a hospital's emergency room

explanation.surface: A grisly vengeance plot set in a hospital, the kind of drama that never loses its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a song, show or story that stays popular year after year, like a tree that never loses its leaves.

clue.text: Pioneering magazine supporting struggle over dope's affection

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes later in the answer

parts.note: Ms. was the pioneering US feminist magazine founded in the 1970s
dope and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A trailblazing magazine backs a campaign over someone's drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the magazine supporting the struggle sits beneath it, and the cannabis comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a warm spot for someone means feeling fond of them, a variant of 'soft spot'.

clue.text: Pelt second cousin, for example

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a cousin is one of your kin, your relatives

explanation.surface: Someone throws things at a second cousin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' reads as a verb, to pelt someone, but it is the noun for an animal's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal's skin with its fur on.

clue.text: Coat dislocated back of guitar player

indicators.note: a dislocated thing is knocked out of its proper place, so the letters move out of order
the back of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

explanation.surface: A guitarist's coat has slipped off the back of their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a part on stage, the same as an actor.

clue.text: Colorado mountain talk
Financial returns in occupancy rate? No more

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the run of letters is read right to left
the letters wanted lie inside the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the last letter of occupancy, all of rate and no, and the first letter of more run together

explanation.surface: A landlord laments that the money from occupancy has dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Financial returns' reads as income, but 'returns' signals the backward reading and 'Financial' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe matters relating to money, so they are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Initially jocular element in slang

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: argon is a chemical element, a noble gas

explanation.surface: Slang that starts with a joke, as if it had a humorous element.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the special vocabulary of a group, much as slang is informal insider language.

clue.text: Health of a water source (a lake)

parts.note: a well is a hole dug to draw water

explanation.surface: The quality of a spring's water, judged by the lake it feeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is a large lake in the Scottish Highlands; the answer runs on into 16-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellness is the state of being in good health, physically and mentally.

clue.text: Broken cane, maybe
Pay back ungodly sum with, er, brie

indicators.note: ungodly means wicked or outrageous, so the words that follow are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly offers cheese to repay an outrageous debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ungodly sum' sounds like a huge amount, but ungodly is the signal and sum is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse someone is to repay them money they have spent.

clue.text: See 13
Crime's true weight

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for true in logic

explanation.surface: A judge weighs how serious a crime really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft, taking another's property, is a criminal offence, so it is an example of a crime.

clue.text: Secret urge: never to employ a Russian writer

indicators.note: to employ something is to hold it within, so the words before contain the answer

parts.note: runs from the last letter of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A hidden longing never to hire a Russian author.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a 19th-century Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Night-flying doohickey?

indicators.note: letters that are flying are scattered through the air and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A gadget, perhaps a drone, that flies after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night-flying' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen hides a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A doohickey is an object whose name escapes you, and 'thing' is the vaguest word for any object.

clue.text: Dated joint affliction besets one

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one part closes in around the other

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned joint complaint troubles a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' seems to describe the affliction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone out of fashion is passé, which is what dated means.

clue.text: Someone not sharing property that's new or remodeled
Ed heads north to infiltrate pious, eccentric Catholic group

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means going up the column, so the name is read upward
to infiltrate is to get inside, so one part is slipped into the other
eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the word before it is put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man named Ed travels north to go undercover in an odd devout Catholic sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Roman Catholic organization of clergy and lay members founded in Spain in 1928.

clue.text: Discredit, or toss out of bed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: expose a claim as false
second, playful meaning: remove someone from a bunk

explanation.surface: Two choices for dealing with someone: ruin their name or turf them out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading, taking the answer as de- plus bunk, a bed on a ship or in a dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk is to show that a belief or claim is false, discrediting it; read literally, the word means taking away a bunk.

clue.text: In the end, layered frozen dessert could be cut into small pieces

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: an ice is a frozen dessert such as sorbet

explanation.surface: A layered ice-cream cake could finally be chopped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice food is to chop it into small cubes.

clue.text: "Kiss and hug" clue sat uncorrected

parts.note: in XOXO sign-offs, O stands for a hug

indicators.note: something left uncorrected is still jumbled, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A crossword clue about kisses and hugs went to print with an error.
explanation.walkthrough: In letters and texts, X is a kiss and O a hug, so 'Kiss and hug' looks like XO; here Kiss is the definition and hug alone gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculate is a formal, Latin-derived verb for kissing.

clue.text: Shoots up part of a letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: Someone shoots up part of a letter, as though it were a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke at the end of a printed letter's main lines.

clue.text: Religious group in the morning, more or less?

explanation.surface: A sect that meets roughly in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Christian community known for plain dress and rejecting much modern technology.

clue.text: Fly (an insect, by the sound of it)

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word spoken the same as the one meant, not spelt the same

parts.note: a flea is a small jumping insect

explanation.surface: A fly, which is an insect, judging by what it sounds like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'insect' suggest the bug, but Fly is the verb meaning run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly from danger is to escape it quickly, the same as to flee.

clue.text: Commuter's cheer in Oregon
Doctor! I have an urgent need

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
I've is the contraction of I have, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A patient cries out to the doctor about something pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a strong inner urge, such as the drive to eat or to succeed.

clue.text: Strangely, these folk fit with something to be considered — it might help you finish solving five of the Across clues

definitions.text: something to be considered — it might help you finish solving five of the Across clues

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters that follow are set out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A puzzle instruction about odd people fitting in with a matter worth weighing.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme key: five Across answers begin with a fish (BASS, PIKE, PERCH, SOLE, CARP) that their wordplay leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle of fish is an idiom for a matter or state of affairs, as in 'a different kettle of fish', and it holds the fish the themed clues need.
